newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst lags on DAX after Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst lags on DAX after Q1 earnings.

text.p: Shares in German chemicals giant Hoechst AG underperformed in early pre-bourse trade on Monday after releasing first-quarter earnings figures that lay somewhat below market expectations.
Its shares were down 30 pfennigs at 66.50 marks ($38.51) at 0720 GMT, while the 30-share IBIS DAX index was breaking records and up 1.15 percent at 3,531.25 points.

Hoechst reported pre-tax earnings of 831 million marks, representing a rise of nine percent after adjustments to reflect special factors. Sales were up at 13.2 billion marks compared with 13.0 billion the previous year.
"Hoechst is dragging the mood here," said a Frankfurt dealer, who said some estimates had forecast Hoechst's pre-tax earnings at well over one billion marks.

Christian Faitz, chemicals analyst at Trinkaus Capital Management, noted that Hoechst's first quarter had been hard to predict because of the restructuring process the company is going through and said the bare data provided by the company needed more analysis.
"Overall, the numbers were slightly disappointing. We had expected slightly higher sales. Of course one must take into account the special factors," Faitz said.
Faitz has a "weak hold" recommendation on Hoechst.
